aiAudit.reason: The diff replaces a per-test `TcpNioConnectionSupport` mock with a field re-initialized to a fresh mock in @BeforeEach, which is the intended promotion pattern. No stubbing, argument matcher or answer exists on this mock, and the only assertions are identity checks (`isSameAs`) against the same instance passed to `connectionSupport(...)` in each test, so no test can now pass for a different reason. Because @BeforeEach creates a new instance per test case, there is no cross-test sharing of accumulated interactions or mutable state and no execution-order dependency. Both call sites were actually replaced, so the duplication was genuinely removed.

Neither test asserts on accumulated interactions or mutable state of the Session mock itself; the only verification, 'Mockito.verify(sessionFactory, Mockito.times(2)).getSession();', targets sessionFactory, which is still created locally in the test body. Both call sites were actually replaced, so the duplication was genuinely removed.

aiAudit.reason: The new private helper `createMockSession(Map<String, TestLsEntry[]> listResults)` creates a fresh `Session` mock per invocation (`Session session = mock(Session.class);`) and re-establishes exactly the same per-path stubs by iterating the supplied map (`when(session.list(entry.getKey())).thenReturn(entry.getValue());`), so no stub, matcher or argument binding is dropped or weakened and no mock instance is shared across tests. All 11 tests reported as sharing the `session.list(...)` stubbing (testLs, testLs_f, testLs_f_R, testLs_f_R_dirs, testLs_None, testLs_1, testLs_1_f, testLs_1_dirs, testLs_1_dirs_links, testLs_1_a_f_dirs_links, testLs_1_a_f_dirs_links_filtered) have their inline `mock(Session.class)` + `when(session.list(...)).thenReturn(...)` lines replaced by a `createMockSession(...)` call, so the duplication was genuinely removed rather than only abstracted. The only incidental changes are statement reordering (e.g. computing `files`/`level1..level3` before the mock) and the use of `Map.of`/`singletonMap`/`HashMap`, which is safe because the stubbed keys are distinct literals, so map iteration order cannot alter matching.

No stub or matcher was dropped or altered (the mock has no stubbing at all; only `addInterceptor` verifications, with `never()` preserved verbatim in both negative-path tests), and every duplicated creation site was actually replaced (no leftover `InterceptableChannel channel = mock();` remains in the diff).
